howToEdit: Every shot lives in the shots list below. Add, remove or rewrite them freely.
act: struggle | grind | win. Each act needs at least 3 shots.
place: where in the home. Add new places to rooms so clips group by room.

style: what kind of shot it is, one of the names in styleLabels (person, body, hands, macro, overhead, pov, low, wide-side, ultrawide, visual-hook). The first shot of every list is a visual-hook shot.
action: what to do, one sentence. feeling: the mood it should read as. tip: one filming tip.
hold: seconds to record (5 gives room to cut 1-3 second pieces). frame: wide | medium | close | detail (detail = no face check).
face: true if your face should be visible. Most good videos are 55-75% shots without your face. cam: propped (default) or handheld.
themes: topics the shot fits. general fits every video. The words that switch on each theme are in themeWords.
id: any short unique name, never reuse one.

acts.name: Struggle
acts.blurb: Show the problem. Slow, heavy, a bit messy.

acts.name: Grind
acts.blurb: Show the effort. Hands busy, eyes focused.

acts.name: Win
acts.blurb: Show the payoff. Light, open, easy.

shots.action: Lean on the counter, run both hands through your hair, and let out a long breath.
shots.tip: Prop the phone at chest height about two steps back, so the counter edge runs along the bottom of the frame.

shots.action: Lie on your back staring at the ceiling, then roll over and pull the pillow over your head.
shots.tip: Stand the phone at the foot of the bed pointing up toward the pillow, with one lamp on, not the big light.

shots.action: Reach out from under the covers and fumble around for your phone without looking.
shots.tip: Put the phone low on the bedside table so your hand slides into the frame from the side.

shots.action: Stare at the screen, rub your eyes with the heels of your hands, then slump back in the chair.
shots.tip: Set the phone on the desk beside the laptop, angled at you, so the screen glow lights your face.

shots.action: Fold your arms on the desk and drop your head onto them, then stay completely still.
shots.tip: Shoot from the side at desk height so we see your back curve, with a messy pile of stuff in front.

shots.action: Sink low into the couch scrolling your phone, only your thumb moving, face totally blank.
shots.tip: Prop the phone on the coffee table at couch height so the camera looks straight at you, not up your nose.

shots.action: Push a half-eaten bowl away and rest your chin on your hand, staring at nothing.
shots.tip: Keep the bowl in the front of the frame and you slightly behind it, phone at table height.

shots.action: POV: open the fridge, look over the shelves for a few seconds, and close it with nothing in your hand.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Lean in close to the mirror and press your fingertips under your tired eyes.
shots.tip: Film over your shoulder into the mirror, and keep the phone out of the reflection.

shots.action: Stand at the window holding a mug in both hands, shoulders dropped, staring out.
shots.tip: Film from the side, not from outside looking in, so the window light falls across your face.

shots.action: Come in the door, drop your bag on the floor, and lean back against the door with your eyes closed.
shots.tip: Prop the phone down the hallway facing the door and start rolling before you come in.

shots.action: Sit on the floor with your back against the couch, knees up, and tip your head back.
shots.tip: Put the phone on the floor a few steps away, tilted up slightly, so the room feels big around you.

shots.action: Click through tabs fast, sigh, and shut the laptop halfway.
shots.tip: Shoot from beside the laptop at eye level so we see your face react, not the screen.

shots.action: Pour coffee into a mug that is already full, notice, and stare at the spill.
shots.tip: Get close to the mug and keep your hands and the pot in frame; put a towel down first.

shots.action: Pull a top out of the closet, frown at it, and toss it on the pile behind you.
shots.tip: Stand the phone on a shelf or chair facing the closet so we see the pile growing.

shots.action: Check the time on your phone, groan, and press your face into a cushion.
shots.tip: Use just one lamp so the room feels late; keep the phone close enough to see the groan.

shots.action: Spread out a few envelopes and receipts, tap numbers into your phone calculator, then put your face in your hands.
shots.tip: Shoot from across the table so the paper mess fills the bottom half of the frame.

shots.action: Sit on the edge of the bed, look around at the mess, and let your shoulders drop.
shots.tip: Prop the phone across the room so the mess and you are both in frame.

shots.action: Crumple an empty snack wrapper in your hand and drop it on top of the others.
shots.tip: Get the phone close to the counter, level with the wrappers, so your hand comes in from above.

shots.action: Sit up in bed with your phone lighting your face, scrolling and blinking slowly.
shots.tip: Keep one soft lamp on behind the phone; even a dark mood needs a little light to film.

shots.action: Sit on the floor to tie your shoes, stop halfway, and lean your head back against the wall.
shots.tip: Put the phone on the floor facing you so the shoes are big in the front of the frame.

shots.action: Splash water on your face, then look up at the mirror, unimpressed.
shots.tip: Film from the side of the sink at shoulder height; wipe drops off the lens before you start.

shots.action: Write a to-do list, cross nothing off, and start doodling in the corner instead.
shots.tip: Hold the phone above the page or prop it on books looking down, so the page fills the frame.

shots.action: Rest your forehead against the window and watch the street, not moving.
shots.tip: Film from slightly behind and to the side so we see your profile and the outside.

shots.action: Reach your hand quickly toward the lens as if to grab the phone, filling the frame in the first second.
shots.tip: Start moving the moment it starts recording: this is the first second of your video.

shots.action: Your hand shoots out from under the covers straight toward the lens to grab the phone.
shots.tip: Start moving the moment it starts recording: this is the first second of your video.

shots.action: Slide a mug or the product straight toward the lens until it almost touches it.
shots.tip: Start moving the moment it starts recording: this is the first second of your video.

shots.action: Close-up of a mug of coffee gone cold, a skin on top, a finger tapping the rim.
shots.tip: Get the phone as close as it will still focus (tap the screen to focus), with light from the side.

shots.action: Overhead: a messy desk covered in papers, a cold mug, and a phone lighting up with notifications.
shots.tip: Hold the phone flat above, pointing straight down, or rest it across two stacks of books.

shots.action: POV: sit on the edge of the bed and look down at your feet on the floor, not getting up.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Low angle from the floor: your feet drag slowly past the camera.
shots.tip: Lay the phone on the floor, leaning back slightly against something, pointing along the floor.

shots.action: Wide from the side: you slumped at the desk, the room dim around you.
shots.tip: Prop the phone across the room, side-on to you, so we see you and the space around you.

shots.action: 0.5x close-up of the pile of dishes in the sink.
shots.tip: Film this one in the Camera app at 0.5x, close to the lens, then tap "Use a clip from my Photos".

shots.action: Close-up of a crowded sink edge, half-used products knocked over.
shots.tip: Get the phone as close as it will still focus (tap the screen to focus), with light from the side.

shots.action: Overhead: bills and receipts spread across the table, one hand pushing them around.
shots.tip: Hold the phone flat above, pointing straight down, or rest it across two stacks of books.

shots.action: POV: your phone in your hand, thumb scrolling an endless feed.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Stretch your arms over your head in the morning light and smile without trying.
shots.tip: Stand beside the window, not in front of it, so the light is on your face.

shots.action: Lean on the counter with a coffee, relaxed, and laugh at something off camera.
shots.tip: Same spot as a struggle shot works great here; the change in mood tells the story.

shots.action: Close the laptop, lean back, and put your hands behind your head.
shots.tip: Leave space above your head for text and keep the desk tidy now.

shots.action: Drop onto the couch, put your feet up, and breathe out with your eyes closed.
shots.tip: Prop the phone across the room so we see the whole couch and you landing on it.

shots.action: Look in the mirror, touch your cheek, and give yourself a small smile.
shots.tip: Face the light, keep the phone at eye level, and leave a little room above your head.

shots.action: Sit down to a plate you made, take the first bite, and nod.
shots.tip: Put the plate front and center with you just behind it; a window beside you is perfect.

shots.action: Wake up before the alarm, sit up easily, and switch it off calmly.
shots.tip: Open the curtains before you film so the room looks like morning.

shots.action: Walk out the door in a good outfit, then glance back with a grin.
shots.tip: Prop the phone in the hallway at chest height and walk away from it.

shots.action: Tick the last box on your list with a flourish and set the pen down.
shots.tip: Get close above the page so the ticks fill the frame.

shots.action: Sip from a mug by the window, eyes closed for a second, shoulders down.
shots.tip: Film from the room side so soft window light falls on your face.

shots.action: Dance a few loose steps to music only you can hear.
shots.tip: Prop the phone far enough back that your arms never leave the frame.

shots.action: Check yourself out in a full-length mirror, turn side to side, and nod.
shots.tip: Film from beside the mirror, not in it, so the phone stays out of the reflection.

shots.action: Hold your notebook or phone up to the camera with a little "see?" look.
shots.tip: Get close and keep what you are holding sharp; tap the screen on it before you start.

shots.action: Open the window, take a deep breath of fresh air, and smile.
shots.tip: Film from the side so the light is on your face, not behind you.

shots.action: POV: open the fridge to a shelf of prepped meals and reach for one.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Curl up reading a book, phone nowhere in sight.
shots.tip: Warm lamp light and a blanket in frame make this feel cozy.

shots.action: Look around the tidy room, hands on hips, satisfied.
shots.tip: Put the phone in a corner so it sees the whole clean room.

shots.action: Read something good on the screen, put a hand on your chest, and do a small fist pump.
shots.tip: Let the screen light your face and keep the camera at eye level.

shots.action: Fall back onto the made bed, arms out, grinning.
shots.tip: Put the phone at the foot of the bed and step back into the frame before you fall.

shots.action: Turn your face slowly toward the window light and let it catch your skin.
shots.tip: Natural light only; turn off the bathroom light for this one.

shots.action: Drop a few notes into a savings jar and pat the lid.
shots.tip: Get close to the jar so the money is easy to see.

shots.action: Sit tall, type calmly with a mug beside you, and smile a little.
shots.tip: Same desk as your struggle shot, but tidy and better lit.

shots.action: Finish the last stretch, sit back on your heels, and smile at the camera.
shots.tip: Prop the phone low so your whole body and the mat are in frame.

shots.action: Walk in with groceries or a gym bag, a bounce in your step, and set them down easily.
shots.tip: Mirror your struggle doorway shot: same angle, opposite energy.

shots.action: Macro close-up of steam rising from a fresh cup in the morning light.
shots.tip: Get the phone as close as it will still focus (tap the screen to focus), with light from the side.

shots.action: Overhead: a full, colourful plate set down on the table.
shots.tip: Hold the phone flat above, pointing straight down, or rest it across two stacks of books.

shots.action: Overhead: a to-do list with every line ticked off, the pen laid beside it.
shots.tip: Hold the phone flat above, pointing straight down, or rest it across two stacks of books.

shots.action: POV: pull the curtains open onto a bright morning.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Low angle from the floor: your feet step out the door with a bounce.
shots.tip: Lay the phone on the floor, leaning back slightly against something, pointing along the floor.

shots.action: Wide from the side: you stretched out on the couch, completely at ease.
shots.tip: Prop the phone across the room, side-on to you, so we see you and the space around you.

shots.action: 0.5x close-up: your products lined up neatly on the shelf.
shots.tip: Film this one in the Camera app at 0.5x, close to the lens, then tap "Use a clip from my Photos".

shots.action: Macro close-up of the savings jar, now full.
shots.tip: Get the phone as close as it will still focus (tap the screen to focus), with light from the side.

shots.action: POV: look down at your phone showing you woke up before the alarm.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Wide from the side: you at a clear desk, working calmly in good light.
shots.tip: Prop the phone across the room, side-on to you, so we see you and the space around you.

shots.action: Open the laptop, crack your knuckles, and start typing fast.
shots.tip: Set the phone at the side of the desk at eye level and fill the frame with you and the laptop.

shots.action: Put your phone face down on the counter and slide it away from you.
shots.tip: Get low and close to the counter so the phone slides out of frame.

shots.action: Plug your phone in, put it face down, and set a book in its place by the bed.
shots.tip: Prop the phone close to the bedside table, at table height, so your hands do the work in frame.

shots.action: Chop vegetables in a steady rhythm, eyes on the board.
shots.tip: Put the phone on a stack of books beside the board, looking down at the knife and your hands.

shots.action: Spoon food into containers lined up in a row and snap the lids on one by one.
shots.tip: Line the containers across the frame from left to right so the row looks satisfying.

shots.action: Write in a notebook, pause, and underline something twice.
shots.tip: Shoot from over your shoulder so we see the page and a bit of your face.

shots.action: Roll out a mat and do slow stretches, breathing out on each one.
shots.tip: Prop the phone low on the floor, a few big steps away, so your whole body fits in the frame.

shots.action: Do five slow squats in the middle of the room, eyes forward.
shots.tip: Put the phone at hip height far enough back to fit you head to toe with space above.

shots.action: Pat serum into your face with your fingertips, slow and unhurried.
shots.tip: Face a window or lamp so the light hits your skin from the front, and keep the phone at face height.

shots.action: Fill a big water bottle at the tap and take a long drink.
shots.tip: Film from the side so the bottle and your face are both in frame.

shots.action: Set a timer on your phone, put it face down, and pick up your pen.
shots.tip: Prop the phone close and looking down at the desk; keep the clutter out of the frame.

shots.action: Dim the lamp, get under the covers, and open a book.
shots.tip: Keep the lamp in the shot or just out of it; warm, low light is the whole mood here.

shots.action: Put the coffee jar back in the cupboard and fill the kettle for tea instead.
shots.tip: Set the phone back far enough that we see you, the cupboard, and the kettle in one shot.

shots.action: Fold laundry on the couch into neat stacks.
shots.tip: Shoot across the stacks so they grow toward the camera.

shots.action: Wipe down the counter in long strokes until it is clear.
shots.tip: Shoot low along the counter so the clean surface catches the light.

shots.action: Flip a flashcard, mouth the answer, and flip the next one.
shots.tip: Sit facing a window or lamp and put the phone at eye height so we see your concentration.

shots.action: Write numbers into a budget notebook and tick each line off.
shots.tip: Prop the phone looking down at the page; a pen and a calculator in frame help.

shots.action: Grab your keys and water bottle and head out the door with purpose.
shots.tip: Prop the phone down the hallway and walk away from it, out the door.

shots.action: Walk past the camera with a mug and a stack of books, eyes forward.
shots.tip: Start rolling with the hallway empty, walk through, and let it go empty again.

shots.action: Put your headphones on, take one deep breath, and lean into the screen.
shots.tip: Get close at eye level with a light in front of you; the breath should read clearly.

shots.action: Set an alarm on your phone and put it face down across the room.
shots.tip: Film from the bed so we watch you walk the phone away.

shots.action: Cross off another day on a calendar or habit tracker with a marker.
shots.tip: Get close so the row of crosses fills the frame, light coming from the side.

shots.action: Pour a scoop of oats into a bowl and level it off with a knife.
shots.tip: Shoot from just above counter height so the pour looks clean.

shots.action: Open the curtains first thing and stand in the light for one slow breath.
shots.tip: Film from inside the room so the light pours toward the camera; tap the screen on your face to fix exposure.

shots.action: Macro close-up of water pouring into a glass.
shots.tip: Get the phone as close as it will still focus (tap the screen to focus), with light from the side.

shots.action: Overhead flat lay: ingredients laid out in neat rows, then your hands start chopping.
shots.tip: Hold the phone flat above, pointing straight down, or rest it across two stacks of books.

shots.action: Overhead: your hand writing a plan for the week in a notebook.
shots.tip: Hold the phone flat above, pointing straight down, or rest it across two stacks of books.

shots.action: POV: look down at your hands lacing up your trainers.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Low angle from the floor: your feet step onto the mat and plant.
shots.tip: Lay the phone on the floor, leaning back slightly against something, pointing along the floor.

shots.action: Wide from the side: you cooking at the counter, steady and focused.
shots.tip: Prop the phone across the room, side-on to you, so we see you and the space around you.

shots.action: 0.5x close-up: your hands typing, the keyboard stretching toward the lens.
shots.tip: Film this one in the Camera app at 0.5x, close to the lens, then tap "Use a clip from my Photos".

shots.action: Macro close-up of one drop of serum landing on your fingertip.
shots.tip: Get the phone as close as it will still focus (tap the screen to focus), with light from the side.

shots.action: POV: open your banking app and move money into savings.
shots.tip: Hold the phone at your eye level, so it sees exactly what you see.

shots.action: Wide from the side: you holding a slow stretch on the floor, the room around you.
shots.tip: Prop the phone across the room, side-on to you, so we see you and the space around you.
